transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
I’ve started going out of my way to avoid any job that involves getting up high. When I absolutely can’t avoid it, I’m barely able to stay up there long enough to do my work.
Can you tell me if you experience excessive anxiety or fear when you're in situations where you're not high up, such as being in crowded places or using public transportation?
No, not at all. I'm completely fine in crowded places or on public transit. This fear of mine is strictly limited to being up high; that's the only thing that gets to me.
Can you describe what specifically happens or what you experience when you're in a high place that makes you feel anxious or fearful?

The second my boot hits a high ladder or I step near an edge, my heart starts pounding, my chest tightens, and my legs feel completely rubbery. Even when I know I'm clipped in and safe, my mind immediately flashes to vivid pictures of me tipping over the edge and falling.
Have you always had this fear of heights, or did it start after a specific incident or experience?

I’ve always had a mild, manageable uneasiness with heights, but it never really interfered with my life or work. That changed about a year ago when I watched a subcontractor nearly fall to his death when a scaffolding plank gave way on my job site. Ever since witnessing that near-miss, this fear has become completely overwhelming and uncontrollable.
Did you experience any significant distress, such as flashbacks, nightmares, or avoidance of reminders, related to the scaffolding incident itself, beyond just the fear of heights that it triggered?

No, I don't have nightmares or flashbacks about the accident itself, and I don't mind talking or thinking about what happened. My anxiety is strictly focused on the physical sensation of being up high and that overwhelming fear of falling over the edge.
